sectors.trend: Pilbara iron ore activity booming; Gateway Resources (GWR.AX) adds 7km gold trend in WA; Bapcor and Metal Hawk among weekly ASX runners. Commodity backdrop supportive but energy policy uncertainty (coal vs renewables) adds a structural overhang.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX benefit from iron ore strength. Gold miners (GWR.AX, NGM.AX) attract rotation as rate uncertainty persists. Energy policy debate (Hanson coal push) could pressure renewable names but support coal-heavy operators.

sectors.trend: Rising rate expectations (headline 9) support NIMs but housing stress (auctions down, 72% of buyers paused) raises credit-risk concerns. ASIC insurance settlement issues add governance risk to insurers.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher-for-longer rates but face elevated NPL risk if housing correction deepens. Insurance names (CGU.AX, WPA.AX) face regulatory scrutiny.

sectors.trend: Australia's 'high bar' for fossil-fuel data centres and Hanson's coal-over-renewables push create policy volatility. Virgin's fuel hedging shields Qantas/Virgin from oil shocks.
sectors.implications: SOL.AX, WES.AX face policy uncertainty. QAN.AX, DLP.AX benefit from hedging. Coal exporters (WDS.AX, BRL.AX) may see political tailwind.

sectors.trend: GLP-1 drugs driving demand shifts (Victoria's Secret +300%); EV uptake accelerating; 'dupe' brands gaining share. Childcare sector in crisis with closures and plunging revenue.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX benefits from global GLP-1/healthcare demand. WES.AX, WTW.AX face margin pressure from dupe-brand competition. Childcare operators (e.g., ECA.AX) under stress.

sectors.trend: SpaceX wireless expansion and AI data centre disruption themes active. Australia's fossil-fuel 'high bar' for data centres could slow domestic build-out. CrowdStrike posts record quarter.
sectors.implications: ASX-listed tech (W1.AX, XRO.AX) face slower data-centre demand. Global tech strength (CRWD, T) provides sentiment support but limited ASX direct exposure.

sectors.trend: Housing market showing correction signals: auction sentiment deteriorating, 72% of buyers paused, 41% regretting the pause. Housing inflation constrains RBA easing.
sectors.implications: Property REITs (VCG.AX, DGP.AX) face occupancy and valuation pressure. Residential builders (GPT.AX, MYR.AX) at risk if correction deepens. Student housing (77) shows resilience at $440k/bed.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA hawkish pivot / delayed rate cuts
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds; favour rate-sensitive financials (CBA.AX, NAB.AX) with strong NIMs; underweight rate-sensitive REITs and growth equities.
Monitor NPL trends at major banks; reduce exposure to residential builders (GPT.AX, MYR.AX); favour defensive consumer staples.
Diversify across energy sub-sectors; monitor One Nation policy influence on federal energy strategy.
Reduce mega-cap tech concentration; rotate into ASX mid-caps and value sectors; maintain cash buffer.
Review exposure to CGU.AX, WPA.AX; favour well-capitalised insurers with strong claims reserves.
Avoid childcare operators; monitor for consolidation opportunities.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain volatile with a modest upward bias. Rate-expectation spikes and housing stress create headwinds, but mining strength and bank NIMs provide support. Expect range-bound trading in ^AXJO with sector rotation into financials and materials. Key risk: any RBA surprise hawkish signal could trigger a 2-3% pullback.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if housing correction is orderly and RBA eases later in 2026. Structural tailwinds: GLP-1 healthcare demand, iron ore resilience, gold as rate hedge. Structural headwinds: energy policy uncertainty, childcare sector decline, potential credit stress. ^AXJO likely to grind higher in a 8,200-8,800 range absent a global shock.
